title: A 185.2dB-FoMs 8.7aFrms Zoomed Capacitance-to-Digital Converter with Chopping-Based kT/C Noise Cancellation and Add-Then-Subtract Phase-Domain Lead-Compensation Technique
problem: VCO-based time-domain delta-sigma capacitance-to-digital converters (CDCs) face kT/C sampling noise exacerbation at reduced oversampling ratios and lack efficient feedforward compensation techniques for VCO's intrinsically fused integrator and quantizer.
motivation: Real-time robotics and drone motion-tracking require high-resolution, low-latency CDCs with energy efficiency for fast MEMS sensor readout (<32µs).
method: The circuit measures capacitance in two stages: a fast rough estimate using SAR (successive approximation register, a binary-search measurement technique), then precise refinement based on oscillator timing (VCO). To reduce thermal noise that worsens at low measurement speeds, it uses chopping—repeatedly flipping the signal to shuffle noise away—requiring only minimal signal amplification, unlike conventional methods that need power-hungry amplifiers. It stabilizes the feedback loop using phase-domain lead-compensation (an 'add-then-subtract' technique for timing adjustments), enabling a stable high-order loop without reducing measurement accuracy and eliminating the need for separate amplifier circuits (OTAs).
key_novelty: Combining chopping for thermal noise cancellation with efficient phase-domain lead-compensation enables high-order oscillator-based measurement without separate amplifier circuits.
contributions: 185.2dB FoMs resolution (8.7aFrms noise equivalent) for capacitance measurement
Chopping-based kT/C noise cancellation reducing required amplification
Add-then-subtract phase-domain lead-compensation for stable high-order loops
Fast measurement time with high energy efficiency suitable for real-time applications
primary_theme: Ultra-low-noise zoomed capacitance-to-digital converter with chopping and phase-domain compensation
